title: OIDC/SSO authentication for JMAP and IMAP
description:
Add OIDC (OpenID Connect) as an authentication backend for the JMAP and IMAP services, enabling enterprise customers to SSO via their corporate IdP (AWS Cognito, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, etc.).

Why this issue exists:
Enterprise buyers on AWS Marketplace expect to authenticate through their existing IdP rather than managing a separate bcrypt credential store. The JMAP server already has bearer token infrastructure — the natural extension is to accept JWT access tokens issued by a configured OIDC provider instead of (or alongside) self-issued tokens.

Scope:
- JMAP: accept Bearer tokens that are JWTs signed by a configured OIDC provider. Validate signature (via JWKS endpoint), expiry, audience, and issuer claims. Extract username from a configurable claim (default: 'email' or 'sub').
- IMAP: SASL OAUTHBEARER (RFC 7628) — the standard mechanism for IMAP+OAuth2/OIDC. Requires STARTTLS to be complete first (blocked on stoa-74b386c0).
- NNTP: out of scope — NNTP has no standard OAuth2/OIDC SASL mechanism; TLS client certs (SASL EXTERNAL) remain the enterprise path for NNTP.
- SAML: out of scope for v1 of this feature — OIDC covers the same IdPs.

Configuration (in [auth] section):

Multiple providers may be listed (e.g. Cognito + Entra for a multi-cloud operator).

Target IdPs to validate against:
- AWS Cognito User Pools
- Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)
- Okta
- Google Workspace

Implementation notes:
- Use the jsonwebtoken or jwt-simple crate for JWT validation
- Fetch JWKS from the provider's well-known endpoint at startup and refresh on 401 from key rotation
- Cache JWKS in memory with a configurable TTL (default: 1 hour)
- Do not store the JWT or any claims in the database — stateless validation only
- Existing bcrypt + self-issued bearer token paths must continue to work alongside OIDC

Acceptance criteria:
- A JMAP client authenticated with a Cognito JWT can list mailboxes and read email
- A JMAP client with an expired or invalid JWT receives 401
- An IMAP client using SASL OAUTHBEARER with a valid OIDC token authenticates successfully
- Existing bcrypt username/password auth continues to work when OIDC is configured
- JWKS rotation does not require a daemon restart
